issues.title: UX: Add breadcrumb navigation to all main views
issues.description:
## Summary
PULSE has no breadcrumb trail anywhere in the application. Users navigating from the
action item list → item detail → post-award → sub-contractor have no visible path
back and must use the browser Back button or top-level navigation menu. This is
particularly disorienting in the Admin area, which has 27 sub-sections.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A Bootstrap breadcrumb component is added to the shared layout (`_Layout.cshtml` or a partial)
- [ ] Breadcrumbs are populated per-view using a ViewData/ViewBag convention (e.g., `ViewData["Breadcrumbs"]`)
- [ ] At minimum, breadcrumbs are implemented for: Dashboard → Item List → Item Detail → each sub-tab (Post Award, Compliance Docs, etc.)
- [ ] Admin area breadcrumbs reflect: Admin Home → Section → Record (e.g., Admin → Users → Edit)
- [ ] Breadcrumbs are rendered as a `<nav aria-label="breadcrumb">` with `<ol class="breadcrumb">` for accessibility
- [ ] The current page is the last breadcrumb item and is not a link (`aria-current="page"`)
- [ ] No existing navigation or layout behavior is broken

issues.title: UX: Add admin dashboard with quick-access to common tasks
issues.description:
## Summary
The PULSE Admin area contains 27 sub-sections accessible only through a flat
navigation menu. Administrators have no at-a-glance view of the system state and
must click through menus to reach common tasks like adding a user, editing a lookup,
or reviewing error logs. There is no summary of recent activity, pending access
requests, or data anomalies.

**Affected area:** `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An Admin Home dashboard page is created at `/Admin/Home/Index`
- [ ] The dashboard displays quick-action cards/tiles for the most common tasks: Manage Users, Manage Lookups, Manage Field Config, Review Error Logs, Review API Keys
- [ ] A "Recent Activity" section shows the last 10 configuration changes (user, action, timestamp) if an audit log is available
- [ ] A "Pending Access Requests" count is displayed if the access request feature is active
- [ ] A "Data Anomalies" count links to the DataAnomalyController if anomalies exist
- [ ] The dashboard is responsive and renders correctly on tablet-sized screens
- [ ] Navigation to any Admin sub-section from the dashboard takes no more than 2 clicks

issues.title: UX: Add feedback and progress indication for data exports
issues.description:
## Summary
Data export operations in PULSE provide no user feedback. The export button is
disabled after click (via `onenlist.btnslinks.disable.js`) and re-enabled via a
cookie polling mechanism (`data-trigger-download` attribute, lines 34–52). This
cookie detection is unreliable — race conditions can leave the button permanently
disabled or re-enabled before the download starts, leaving the user with no
indication of whether the export worked.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Web/wwwroot/scripts/onenlist.btnslinks.disable.js`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When an export is triggered, a non-blocking status message appears (e.g., "Preparing your export…")
- [ ] The status message is replaced with "Download ready" or dismissed automatically once the file download begins
- [ ] If the export fails (server error), a user-visible error message is shown (not just a console log)
- [ ] The export button is reliably re-enabled after the download completes or fails
- [ ] The cookie-based re-enable mechanism is replaced with a more reliable approach (e.g., `fetch` with blob response, or a server-sent status endpoint)
- [ ] Existing export functionality is not broken for any export type

issues.title: Add a uniqueness constraint to LookupItem_PscCodeToSpendCat
issues.description:
_Follow-up from the lookup architecture review (#398). Source: the project backlog docs._

### Problem
`LookupItem_PscCodeToSpendCat` defines only FK constraints (all `ClientSetNull`) and **no unique index** (`OneNListContext.cs:617-635`). **DB-verified:** the physical table has only the clustered PK on `ID` — no unique constraint, no FK indexes — and currently holds **97 rows with 0 duplicate `(FK_PscCode, FK_Spending_Category, FK_Organization_ID)` combinations**, so a unique index can be added now without a cleanup step. Without it, duplicate mappings can be inserted and produce ambiguous/doubled goal resolution. The 2026 VendorId mapping already proves the pattern (`UX_Cage_Prime_Org`, `OneNListContext.cs:1566-1568`).

### Proposed change
Add a unique composite index on `(FK_PscCode, FK_Spending_Category, FK_Organization_ID)` via Fluent config + a SQL migration (guard with a pre-check in case PROD differs). Update the CRUD sproc / `SaveOrUpdate` path to upsert rather than blind-insert.

### Affected files
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListContext.cs` (Fluent config)
- New SQL migration under `Source/Migrations/<next-version>/`
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/PscCodeMappingController.cs`

### Rough effort
M.

### Severity
High (D2)

issues.title: Introduce repeatable, idempotent lookup seeding
issues.description:
_Follow-up from the lookup architecture review (#398). Source: the project backlog docs._

### Problem
The entire lookup layer is seeded by hand-run SQL scripts + a `.bak` restore — there are **no `HasData` calls** in `OnModelCreating` (`OneNListContext.cs:160-1591`) and no programmatic seeder. This has already caused cross-environment lookup-ID drift (commit `9682475d`, "Fixed issue with lookup anomalies between DREN and QA"). New environments and the Service Code CSV import depend on the right scripts being applied in the right order.

### Proposed change
Define the canonical lookup *types* (and fixed system items) as idempotent seed data — either EF `HasData` for stable `Lookup` rows, or a versioned re-runnable `MERGE`-based SQL seed invoked at deploy. Document the seed order for Service Code types + goal-map CSV import so a fresh environment reaches a known lookup state in one repeatable step.

### Affected files
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListContext.cs` (if `HasData`)
- New seed script(s) under `Source/Migrations/`
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/PscCodeMappingController.cs` (CSV import order/docs)

### Rough effort
L.

### Severity
Med (D3)

issues.title: Notify users when records are updated / provide a recently-updated records list
issues.description:
## Customer request
> "Would it be possible to set up some kind of alert to notify us when records are updated, or to obtain a list of recently updated records?"

Two related capabilities: (A) a **list/report of recently-updated records**, and (B) an **alert/notification when records are updated**. They're framed as alternatives — recommend delivering (A) first (small, high value) and treating (B) as a follow-on phase because it requires infrastructure decisions.

## What already exists (build on, don't reinvent)
- **Per-record timestamps:** `OneNList.ModifiedDate` / `ModifiedBy` are populated on update (`OneNListContext.cs:731-732`, DB default `getdate()`; set via `OneNItemUpdateHelper`). This is the simplest source for "recently updated."
- **Reporting view:** `BO_View_OneNList` already aggregates action fields for list/report queries.
- **Analytics sproc pattern:** `GetEndUserAnalytics_Totals/_ChangesByType/_ChangesByUser` (`StoredProcedureService.cs:518-540`, surfaced at `/Admin/UserAnalytics`) is a good template for a change-summary query.
- **Change-log tables exist but are NOT populated:** `TableChangeLogSummary` / `TableChangeLogDetail` entities are mapped (`OneNListContext.cs` ~1489-1519) but no code writes to them. Field-level change history is therefore not currently available without new write logic or triggers.
- **Email is a stub:** `EmailService.SendEmailAsync` returns `Task.CompletedTask` with no SMTP (`App_Start/IdentityConfig.cs:11-17`, registered `Program.cs:128`). `eMetricType.Email` enum exists but is unused.
- **SignalR exists** (`Hubs/ProgressHub.cs`, `Helpers/ProgressNotifier.cs`) — currently only for bulk-progress; could power in-app notifications.
- **No background/scheduled job framework** (no `IHostedService`/Hangfire/Quartz) — a digest/scheduled email would need one added.
- **API project** (`Source/OneNListApp.API`) exposes specific history views by API key but has **no** generic "modified since X" endpoint.

## Recommended phased scope

### Phase 1 — Recently-updated records list (low effort, satisfies request B-as-list)
- Add a stored proc / view query: actions where `ModifiedDate >= @cutoff`, scoped by organization (respect existing org multi-tenancy filter), returning PO Control #, Title, ModifiedBy, ModifiedDate, status.
- Surface it as a filterable admin/list page (reuse the action list table styling) and/or a parameterized API endpoint (e.g. `GET /api/RecentlyUpdated?sinceDays=7`) guarded by the existing API-key check.
- Acceptance: a user can see/pull all records in their org updated within a chosen window (default 7 days), sortable by ModifiedDate.

### Phase 2 — Update alerts/notifications (larger; needs decisions)
- Implement real notification delivery. Options:
  - **In-app** via the existing SignalR hub (no SMTP needed).
  - **Email digest** — requires implementing `EmailService` with an SMTP/relay (gov-approved) + a scheduled job (new `IHostedService`) to send a periodic "records updated since last digest" summary, leveraging `eMetricType`.
- Optional: a subscription/preferences table so users opt into which orgs/fields trigger alerts.
- If field-level ("what changed") detail is required (not just "record X was updated"), add population of `TableChangeLogSummary/Detail` (SaveChanges interceptor or DB triggers) — currently empty.

## Decisions needed before Phase 2 (open questions)
1. **Delivery channel:** in-app (SignalR) vs email vs both?
2. If email: is an approved SMTP/relay available in the gov environment, and what cadence (real-time vs daily/weekly digest)?
3. **Granularity:** "record was updated" (use `ModifiedDate`) vs "these fields changed" (requires populating the change-log tables)?
4. **Scope/recipients:** all updates in an org, or only specific statuses/fields, and who receives them?

## Affected files (indicative)
- `Source/OneNListApp.Service/StoredProcedureService.cs` + `IStoredProcedureService.cs` (new query)
- new SQL migration under `Source/Migrations/<next-version>/` (sproc/view; optionally change-log triggers)
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/...` new list page/controller (Phase 1)
- `Source/OneNListApp.API/...` new endpoint (Phase 1, optional)
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/App_Start/IdentityConfig.cs` (implement EmailService), `Program.cs` (register hosted service), `Hubs/ProgressHub.cs` (Phase 2)

## Rough effort
Phase 1: S–M. Phase 2: M–L (depends on channel + digest decisions).

_Source: codebase review of change-tracking, ModifiedDate, EmailService, SignalR, and the API project._
